openwrt_wiki.versionen_support_v2: Atheros ar71xx platform. Box side panel lists WNDR3700v2, also sold as WNDRMAC-100PES, WNDR3700-100PRS
openwrt_wiki.WNDR37AV: Netgear has sold a number of WNDR3700v2 units in boxes marked WNDR37AV. The hardware is exactly identical to version 2 (even to the point of many users finding a router physically labeled "WNDR3700" or "WNDR3700v2" inside of a box labeled "WNDR37AV").
openwrt_wiki.versionserkennung: The v2 revision may not be shown on the router bottom label. V1 and v2 seem to share the same EAN barcodes. If you have the original box, look under "Package Contents" it will say "N600 Wireless Dual Band Gigabit Router (WNDR3700v2)" for version 2, and just "WNDR3700" for version 1. The Netgear firmware GUI shows the "Hardware Version" in the "Maintenance" section under "Router Status". Also, the OEM version version for v1 is 1.0.4.x and higher, while v2 is 1.0.1.x or less.
openwrt_wiki.installation_oem_gui: stock WNDR3700 GUI, factory.img; Non North American users will get an warning regarding that OpenWrt identifies itself an NA, ignore
openwrt_wiki.installation_tftp: static 192.168.1.x; hold 'System Restore' button on the underside while powering on until power led steadily blinks green; upload .img via TFTP; router will not accept the firmware when the filename is too long, firmware.img should work; power led off during flashing, then orange for some time, then green
openwrt_wiki.installation_seriell: Interrupt U-Boot, maybe 'protect off all', fsload, TFTP server on 192.168.1.1; V2: openwrt-ar71xx-generic-wndr3700v2-squashfs-factory.img
openwrt_wiki.installation_nmrpflash: On 3700v2, you can also install a factory image using nmrpflash (see delay issue)
openwrt_wiki.nmrpflash_v2: nrmpflash works with 3700v2. Don't reboot when the program told you so: device continues to write the flash for about 30s; wait about 1min before rebooting, otherwise corrupted memory and the device won't boot
openwrt_wiki.switch: Firmware 24.10.3 (and earlier) use swconfig for this device, not DSA; issue with internal switch: traffic to a wifi client sometimes no longer routed, advice: uncheck 'learning and aging' (ticket 13612)
openwrt_wiki.switch_ports: Numbers 0-3 are Ports 4 to 1 as labeled on the unit, 5 is the internal connection to the router itself
openwrt_wiki.gehaeuse_oeffnen: Torx (T-8); two screws visible on the bottom; four more screws under the rubber feet (not glued)
openwrt_wiki.serial: Internal J1 4-pin connector. 3.3V serial port voltage. Do not connect the 3.3V line. 115200 8N1, no flow control. Pinout table only for v1: Pin1 3.3V, Pin2 TX, Pin3 RX, Pin4 GND
openwrt_wiki.jtag: Internal J3 connector, 14 pins (TRST, TDI, TDO, TMS, TCK, RST, NC, 3.3VDC; even pins GND)
openwrt_wiki.ram_mod_v2: More and more people report serious issues after correctly replacing ram chips on WNDR3700V2; users are advised to stay away from extending RAM on WNDR3700V2; 333 MHz chips do not work with wndr3700v2 (eko.one.pl)
openwrt_wiki.antennen_mod_v2: Revision 2 only has U.FL connectors for the 5 GHz antennas (PJ2 and PJ4), while the 2.4 GHz connectors are replaced with dummy connectors (presumably Hirose testing connectors). For revision 2 the PJ5 and PJ6 connectors will have to be bypassed and the coax cable soldered directly to the PCB.
bekannte_probleme: Wifi stopped working after a while (fixed in AA 12.09, ticket 11894)
WNDR3700v2: Problems with internal switch causing traffic to a particular wifi client to be ignored (workaround present, ticket 13612)
Failed to stop TX DMA messages in syslog (harmless in AA 12.09+)
openwrt_wiki.recovery: TFTP recovery by Netgear u-boot: press and hold RESET as soon as switch LEDs light up until power LED flashes orange then green; TFTP to 192.168.1.1; factory.img or Netgear firmware, not sysupgrade; flashing takes several minutes; bad firmware may enter TFTP recovery automatically (power led blinking slowly)
openwrt_wiki.failsafe: when the power LED changes from steady orange to blinking green press any button (WPS, Wifi or reset) during the next two seconds

openwrt_git_antennen.v2_text: the wndr3700v2 and later revisions were unaffected by the missing bits [5 GHz], as there is no demultiplexer present in the later designs. The WNDR3700v2 and later have just six antennae. Four of those are printed on the circuit board and serve the 2.4GHz radio. Whereas the remaining two are special 5GHz Rayspan Patch Antennae which are directly connected to the 5GHz radio.

deviwiki._text: N600 Wireless Dual Band Gigabit Router; Simultaneous Dual-Band, Gigabit Ethernet; Estimated date of release per Google Trends; Default hardware for the CeroWrt bufferbloat research project; The AR9220 is a 2.4GHz and 5GHz Dual-band radio, the AR9223 2.4GHz only; "Version 2 changes the board layout, replacing the 5GHz onboard antennae with two Rayspan 'meta-material' off board 'patch' antennae. Rayspan was liquidated by its investors and the Rayspan patents were purchased by Tyco Electronics in Q1 2011. FCC exhibits show Rayspan antennae in 2010 Oct 05 filings, but not in earlier and later WNDR3700v2 filings."; Flash Macronix MX25L12845E 128Mb Serial Flash; Review SmallNetBuilder 31396; Galerie WNDR3700v2 019-027.jpg; SupportPage vs_id=17703

lauf.notiz: Gluon-Image netgear-wndr3700-v2 = OpenWrt netgear_wndr3700-v2 (ath79/generic). Ausgewertet: ToH-Dump + Live-hwdata, OpenWrt-Wiki (gemeinsame Seite v1-v5, Rohtext aus Lauf netgear-wndr3700), OpenWrt-Commits (ar71xx 2011, ath79 2018, Antennen 2020, Board-Detect 2015, Umbenennung 2020), DTS/dtsi/generic.mk, Gluon-Target und Commit 374b81d (v2022.1), DeviWiki (= WikiDevi-Spiegel), FCC PY308300092 v2-Exhibits: Änderungsschreiben 2010-09/2010-10, Außen-/Innenfotos 2010 und 2011, Handbuch 2010, Testbericht 15E. Werkstatt: nichts zu v2. Ergebnis: innen, 12 V 2.5 A Hohlstecker Mitte plus (Maß offen), kein PoE, 5x Gigabit, 1x USB 2.0, 2x2 b/g/n + 2x2 a/n, 6 interne Antennen (4x 2.4 GHz gedruckt, 2x 5 GHz Rayspan-Patch), 16 MB NOR / 64 MB RAM, serielle Stiftleiste J1 115200 3.3 V (Pinbelegung nur für v1 belegt), kein Lüfter, v2 oft nicht auf dem Typenschild.
